alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction causing viral rebound
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70% and advise using valproic acid instead. Patient was suppressed (<50 copies/mL) in September 2025 but now has detectable VL 1,240 copies/mL after carbamazepine was added 2 weeks ago. Adherence is reported good, making subtherapeutic DTG from this interaction the likely cause of viral rebound. The patient is already on valproic acid, so carbamazepine was duplicative and avoidable.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine and manage seizures with valproic acid monotherapy or a non-interacting antiepileptic. Repeat viral load in 2–3 months after addressing the interaction.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), with symptoms of ataxia, nystagmus, tremor, dizziness, and headaches. Sodium is 128 mmol/L, consistent with carbamazepine-induced SIADH. The clinician plans dose reduction, but given the severe interaction with DTG, discontinuation in favour of valproic acid is preferred over dose adjustment. Concurrent valproate may also complicate management.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine rather than dose-reducing. Monitor sodium and neurological symptoms. Repeat carbamazepine level only if tapering rather than stopping.

alerts.title: Detectable VL requires enhanced adherence and repeat
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for VL >50 copies/mL on DTG-based ART, clinicians should provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects affecting adherence, and repeat VL in 2–3 months. The clinician's plan does not mention enhanced adherence counselling or a repeat VL timeline. The likely cause (carbamazepine-DTG interaction) should be addressed first, but the guideline-mandated response is incomplete.

evidence.recommended_action: Add enhanced adherence support and schedule repeat viral load in 2–3 months after resolving the carbamazepine-DTG interaction.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT with dual hepatotoxic drugs
alerts.message: ALT is 68 U/L (above normal). Patient is on both sodium valproate and carbamazepine, both of which are hepatotoxic. Carbamazepine was started 2 weeks ago, and recent onset of transaminitis temporally supports drug attribution. DTG and TDF can also cause hepatotoxicity but are less likely given long-term stability. The clinician's plan does not address the elevated ALT.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine (also required for DTG interaction). Repeat ALT and LFTs after stopping. Investigate other causes if ALT persists or worsens.
